375792.title: The collapsibility conjecture for prism complexes of ample sets
375792.literal_statement:
Let $U$ be a Cartesian product and let $S\subseteq U$ be an ample set. Write $\operatorname{Box}(S)$ for the boxes associated with $S$, and let $||\operatorname{Box}(S)||$ denote their prism complex. **Collapsibility conjecture.** The prism complex

$$
||\operatorname{Box}(S)||
$$

of each ample set $S\subseteq U$ is collapsible. This strengthens the contractibility result proved in the paper; the conjecture is presented after noting that collapsibility is known for binary ample sets, while the general case remains unresolved.

375976.title: Two disjoint abelian sets small-doubling conjecture
375976.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a torsion-free group, and let $S$ be a nonempty finite subset of $G$ written as

$$
S=A\cup B,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are disjoint abelian sets. Write $S^2=\{s_1s_2:s_1,s_2\in S\}$ and let $\langle S\rangle$ denote the subgroup generated by $S$.

**Two-set small-doubling conjecture.** If $|S^2|\leq 3k-3$, then $\langle S\rangle$ is abelian.

This conjecture is proposed as a possible extension of the preceding results on small doubling in torsion-free groups. Its status is not resolved in the source.

366560.title: Gajarsky–Pilipczuk–Toruńczyk conjecture on cliquewidth obstruction classes via walls
366560.literal_statement:
For a graph class $\mathscr{C}$, write $\mathscr{C}$ transduces a class $\mathscr{D}$ when the class is obtainable by the relevant first-order transduction. A graph class has **unbounded cliquewidth** when its cliquewidth is not bounded.

**Gajarsky–Pilipczuk–Toruńczyk's cliquewidth obstruction conjecture.** A class of graphs $\mathscr{C}$ has unbounded cliquewidth if and only if $\mathscr{C}$ transduces a class $\mathscr{D}$ that contains some subdivision of every wall.

Together with the corresponding linear-cliquewidth statement, this conjecture would characterize bounded cliquewidth through forbidden transduction patterns. The survey presents it as open.

366644.title: Sulanke's conjecture on 3-Narayana distributions of tableau statistics
366644.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{SYT}(n^3)$ denote the set of standard Young tableaux of rectangular shape $(n,n,n)$, and let $b_{r,s}$ denote the tableau statistics used in the source. Define

$$
\st_1=b_{1,2}+b_{2,2}+b_{2,3}-2,\qquad \st_2=b_{1,1}+b_{1,3}+b_{2,3}-1.
$$

A statistic has a **$3$-Narayana distribution** when its distribution on $\operatorname{SYT}(n^3)$ is the corresponding $3$-Narayana distribution.

**Sulanke's conjecture.** On $\operatorname{SYT}(n^3)$, each of the statistics $\st_1$ and $\st_2$ has a $3$-Narayana distribution.

The statement is attributed to Sulanke. The source proves the assertion for $\st_2$ using a bijection, while the assertion for $\st_1$ remains a conjecture; therefore the combined conjecture remains open.

366670.title: The sumset bounds conjecture for sets with control
366670.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set with control $ba$, meaning that it satisfies the control hypotheses introduced in the paper. For $b5>0$, write $X\gg_b5 Y$ to mean that $X$ is bounded below by a positive constant depending on $b5$ times $Y$. **The sumset bounds conjecture.** If $A$ has control $ba$ then, for any $b5>0$, 

$$
\left\lvert A-A\right\rvert\gg_b5 ba^{-1+b5}\left\lvert A\right\rvert
$$

and

$$
\left\lvert A+A\right\rvert\gg_b5 ba^{-1+b5}\left\lvert A\right\rvert.
$$

These bounds would improve the previously known estimates for difference and sum sets of controlled sets; the surrounding discussion presents them as a natural conjectural strengthening, while the paper does not provide a resolution.

366716.title: The real polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa inverse conjecture
366716.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite set. If $\xi\in\mathbb{R}$ is transcendental and $K_1,K_2\geqslant 2$ satisfy

$$
|A+A|\leqslant K_1|A|\quad\textrm{and}\quad |A+\xi A|\leqslant K_2|A|,
$$

then
**The real polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture.**

$$
(\log K_1)(\log K_2)\gg \log |A|.
$$

This conjectures the analogous estimate over the real numbers to the function-field result proved in the paper, asserting that simultaneous additive and multiplicative-translate structure forces the set to be small unless the doubling parameters are large. The source does not provide evidence that the real-number statement has been resolved.

366804.title: Markov polynomial Newton-polygon saturation conjecture
366804.literal_statement:
Let $\rho=a/b$ be a rational number, and let $\Delta_{a/b}$ be the Newton polygon of the numerator of the Markov polynomial $M_\rho(x,y,z)$, consisting of the integer points $i,j\geq0$ satisfying

$$
\frac{i}{a}+\frac{j}{b}\geq1,\qquad i+j\leq a+b-1.
$$

**Saturation conjecture.** The terms appearing in the numerator of $M_\rho$ are precisely those corresponding to the integer lattice points in $\Delta_\rho$. The conjecture is an equivalent explicit formulation of the assertion that all coefficients associated with lattice points of the Newton polygon are positive; the source gives no resolution.

366942.title: The wedge-of-spheres conjecture for noncrossing parking function posets
366942.literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated complex reflection group of rank $n$ and Coxeter number $h$. Let $\operatorname{Park}^{\mathrm{NC}}(W)$ denote its noncrossing parking function poset, let $\overline{\operatorname{Park}^{\mathrm{NC}}(W)}$ be its proper part, and let $\Omega$ denote the order complex.

**Wedge-of-spheres conjecture.**

$$
\Omega\left(\overline{\operatorname{Park}^{\mathrm{NC}}(W)}\right)\simeq \left(\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\right)^{\vee (h-1)^n}.
$$

This conjecturally extends the known result for finite real reflection groups to well-generated complex reflection groups, describing the topology of the noncrossing parking function poset as a wedge of spheres.
